home.answerLabel: There is a name for all of this
home.title: Ser Poder
home.leadStrong: The world taught us to HAVE power. But no one taught us to BE it.
home.lead: Ser Poder means not depending on what you have in order to recognize who you are. It means finding within yourself a potency that does not vanish when roles, achievements, relationships or recognition change.
home.thesisP1: For more than 25 years I worked alongside capable, recognized and successful people. People who had earned roles, influence, results and everything we usually associate with power.
home.thesisP2: But something did not add up. Some lost their own potency the moment they left a position. Others, even surrounded by recognition, never came to feel truly powerful.
home.thesisP3: That is when one question became unavoidable: if power disappears when whatever confirms it changes, does that power really belong to us?
home.thesisP4: Ser Poder was born out of that restlessness, as an investigation into the distance between what we achieve and the potency we manage to recognize and sustain within ourselves.
home.q1: Why do people who have power seem to lose it when they leave roles, titles or positions?
home.q2: Why do so many others, even surrounded by recognition, influence and performance, not feel truly powerful?
home.q3: And why do some people, with no roles, titles or recognition at all, reveal a potency that seems to depend on none of it?
home.ecpTitle: Out of the investigation came the Conscious Structure of Power
home.ecpP1: The three questions revealed that the experience of power cannot be explained by what a person owns. It is organized in the relationship between who that person is, the context they live in and the way they move inside it.
home.ecpP2: From that understanding came the Conscious Structure of Power, the ECP: Andrea Eboli's original method for crossing the distance between HAVING power and BEING power.
home.ecpP3: The ECP articulates three inseparable dimensions (Identity, Context and Movement) and offers a path to recognize where we hand over our potency, understand what influences us and choose how to act.
home.ecpQuote: It is not a formula for controlling life. It is a structure for not disappearing inside it.
home.dimensionsTitle: The three dimensions of the ECP
home.vocabularyLead: Every idea in the thesis with a name of its own.
home.newsletterLead: Observations on human behavior, conscious leadership, identity and Ser Poder.
audienceDenial: It is not for those who believe they need help.
audienceAffirmation: It is for those who do not need it.
For those who are strong, capable and powerful.
For those who know how to decide, achieve, sustain, resolve and move forward.
For those who became a reference for everyone else, and still depend on the title, the result, the recognition, the control or the roles they occupy to recognize their own power.
audiencePivot: SER PODER is for those who have achieved a great deal on the outside and began to notice that this does not guarantee power on the inside.
Not to give up what they have achieved.
But to stop depending on those achievements to know who they are.
audienceTurn: Because perhaps your next step is not to achieve even more.
It is to stop needing everything you achieved in order to feel powerful.
audienceClose: SER PODER is not born of weakness.
It is born when someone who learned to handle everything realizes that TER PODER, to have power, is not the same as SER PODER, to be power.

aboutPage.headline: Founder of the Academia do Poder. She investigates the new relationships between power, identity and leadership in contemporary life.
aboutPage.p1: Andrea Eboli is a researcher, author, professor and founder of the Academia do Poder. She investigates the new relationships between power, identity and leadership in contemporary life.
aboutPage.questionsLabel: The three questions behind the investigation
aboutPage.q1: Why do people who have power seem to lose it when they leave roles, titles or positions?
aboutPage.q2: Why do so many others, even surrounded by recognition, influence and performance, not feel truly powerful?
aboutPage.q3: And why do some people, with no roles, titles or recognition at all, reveal a potency that seems to depend on none of it?
aboutPage.p2: With an international academic path, a master's degree, a doctorate and more than two decades of executive experience, Andrea brings research and practice together to propose a new understanding of contemporary power and conscious leadership.
aboutPage.p3: Creator of the Conscious Structure of Power (ECP), Andrea turns this investigation into a practical path for people and leaders to cross the distance between having power and recognizing their own potency.
aboutPage.quote: The world has changed. So have the relationships of power. And the way we occupy, sustain and live power must change with it.
experiences: 17 years of executive leadership at Natura &Co.
Master's degree and doctorate from Swiss Business School
Further education at Harvard and NYU
Forbes Business Council member and contributor at forbes.com
aboutPage.galleryFallbackAlt: Andrea Eboli at one of the stages, gatherings and behind the scenes shown in the gallery

articlesQuestionsPage.headline: Real questions and reflections on power, identity and the way we are living, to widen the view and strengthen awareness and inner power.
articlesQuestionsPage.questionsP1: When we begin a journey of personal growth, new questions become part of the path, and we do not always find ready answers.
articlesQuestionsPage.questionsP2: Human Questions is a space for reflection and provocation around those questions, grounded in the principles of the Conscious Structure of Power (ECP). More than offering certainties, each answer invites you to widen your view and find more conscious paths.
articlesQuestionsPage.askPrompt: Didn't find your question here? Send it in. It may inspire one of the next answers.
articlesQuestionsPage.articlesP1: These articles are born where research, theoretical references and lived experience meet. Questions, perceptions and contributions from the people who take part in studies, gatherings and conversations around the ECP.
articlesQuestionsPage.articlesP2: Here, knowledge is not presented as something finished. It is built collectively, tested against real life and expanded with every new exchange. The sources behind each reflection are cited in the texts themselves.

evidence.label: Research and experience
evidence.intro: Ser Poder is built and validated where research meets experience: the research gathers the evidence that supports its hypotheses, while the Confraria Let's Be takes the method into real life, making it possible to observe its application, its effects and the learning it generates in different contexts. Together they connect theory, data and practice, keeping the method in constant evolution.
evidence.quote: The research reveals the patterns. The Confraria puts the method into practice.

researchPage.title: ECP Research
researchPage.headline: The evidence that supports the hypotheses of Ser Poder.
researchPage.crossBody: The Confraria Let's Be takes the ECP into real conversations.
researchPage.stat1Label: agree it is possible to have plenty of external power and still not feel fulfilled.
researchPage.stat2Label: swing between periods of full delivery and moments of searching for a pause or reconnection.
researchPage.stat3Label: chose themselves when asked who comes to mind as a powerful person.
researchPage.dimensionsLead: The ECP reads power through three dimensions. The research shows what happens inside each one.
researchPage.dimIdentityFact1: 90.1% say they are clear about their own values. At the same time, 53.6% adapt who they are to match what is expected of them.
researchPage.dimIdentityFact2: Only 15.4% associate power with having clarity about who you are.
researchPage.dimContextFact1: 84.6% notice which environments strengthen or weaken who they are. Even so, 64% often feel captured by other people urgencies.
researchPage.dimContextFact2: Only 8.9% associate power with reading situations clearly.
researchPage.dimMovementFact1: 59.6% say they know what they need to do and still do not act. The most cited brake is fear of conflict, with 32.8%.
researchPage.dimMovementFact2: 52.8% feel their life is driven more by external demands than by their own choices.
researchPage.dimensionsClose: And the search for a path exists before the method has a name: 71.2% believe a practical direction would help turn awareness into concrete change, and 71.7% report high or total interest in a structured path.
researchPage.method: Quantitative research on an online panel, with 403 professionally active respondents aged 25 to 55, across Brazil. Fieldwork in 2026, with a margin of error of about 4.9 percentage points. Women are 59.6% of the sample and the Southeast region accounts for 64.3%.
researchPage.chartsLead: Four readings of the same 403 respondents, in the order the argument builds.
researchPage.chartIdeasSubtitle: Ideas most associated with power, up to three answers per person. The top four are all external. The four the ECP calls inner power appear far below.
researchPage.ideaStatus: Having a position, title or status
researchPage.ideaClarity: Having clarity about who you are
researchPage.chartRefTitle: Who people think of when they think of power
researchPage.chartRefSubtitle: Single answer. Almost six in ten think first of someone highly visible. And in the open question, where they had to write a name, only 1% wrote their own.
researchPage.refPublic: A public, media or highly visible figure
researchPage.refClose: Someone close, from family, work or daily life
researchPage.chartGapTitle: What they declare and what they live
researchPage.chartGapSubtitle: In every ECP dimension the capability is declared high. The next question, about what the person actually lives, returns a different number. That distance is what the method addresses.
researchPage.gapIdentityDeclared: Have clarity about their own values
researchPage.gapIdentityLived: Adapt who they are to match what is expected of them
researchPage.gapContextDeclared: Notice which environments strengthen or weaken who they are
researchPage.gapContextLived: Often feel captured by other people's urgencies and demands
researchPage.gapMovementDeclared: Manage to turn clarity into concrete decisions
researchPage.gapMovementLived: Know what they need to do and still do not act
researchPage.gapFulfilmentDeclared: Feel their own strength comes from within
researchPage.gapFulfilmentLived: Still feel the urge to achieve external power
researchPage.chartChoiceTitle: When the alternative is on the table
researchPage.chartChoiceSubtitle: Forced choice between four profiles: which one looks like the most powerful person. The profile that brings together the three ECP dimensions beats identity on its own, but external recognition still leads.
researchPage.choiceRecognition: Someone with high public recognition, influence and resources
researchPage.choiceSocial: Someone with strong social intelligence, who reads environments well
researchPage.choiceTriad: Someone with clarity about themselves, who reads the context and acts coherently
researchPage.choiceIdentity: Someone with deep clarity about who they are, their values and their limits
